metric.tcIdle: Town Center idle before Castle Age (estimated)

benchmarks.note: Villagers = starting ones plus those produced by the Town Center, with the queue simulated until Castle Age (after that, with several Town Centers, it is approximate). Idle time is estimated from gaps between queue commands; Loom and age-ups count as busy. Civ bonuses that change these timings (Persians, Malay, Goths, Portuguese, Chinese, Mayans, Bengalis) are applied.

training.title: How to train
training.intro: What the site measures in your games, what to do with it, and the outside tools worth your time. All free.

site.title: What the site does for you

items.name: Your numbers against the division
items.what: Every league game has its recording read by the site, no AI: age-up times, villagers at 10, 15 and 20 minutes, Town Center idle time, first military unit and actions per minute. The table on your profile and on the analysis compares you with the median of your division and the one above. The training focus picks, out of those, the number that fell behind the most.

items.name: AI match analysis
items.what: Three a day, free. The AI gets your numbers and the division's and writes what decided the game and what to train. Request it from the match list on your profile.

items.name: Sparring in the league
items.what: On your division page, click I want to train. Whoever is available shows up in the list for 2 hours; when one of you opens the lobby in the game, the Join lobby button appears and opens the game straight into it. Players from the division above can offer to mentor.

order.title: What to train, in order
items: Pick one build order and repeat it until it runs without thinking. The sites below have the common ones with the villager split at each step.
Play and look at the table: Town Center idle time and villagers at 10 minutes are the two numbers that separate divisions the most. Fix those before thinking about micro.
When your Feudal Age numbers reach the median of the division above, move on to the Castle Age timing.
Request an AI analysis on the losses you did not understand, not on every game. A practice game with someone in your division is worth more than one more ranked game.

items.name: Interactive Build Order Guide
items.what: In-game scenarios that teach 10 build orders step by step and grade you at the end. Search for it by name in the game's Mod Center. Unmaintained since 2020, still the reference.

items.name: IdleTC
items.what: Build orders with the villager split at each step and a compact view to keep open while playing. Free, no account.

items.name: Build Order Guide
items.what: Catalog and editor of build orders, with the expected age-up times.

items.name: AoE2 Hotkeys Practice
items.what: Sequence and speed drills in the browser. Loads your hotkey file from the game. Open source.

items.name: Villager Trainer
items.what: Villager hotkey drills in the browser, without the game open.

items.name: Hotkey course (KeyCombiner)
items.what: Table of every hotkey in the game plus a 30-lesson course. Link to the AoE Zone thread.

items.name: Art of War
items.what: The official challenges, in the game menu. Start there: economy, micro and siege, with medals by time.

items.name: Micro Wars
items.what: Micro scenarios for DE (archers, galleys, towers, siege). Search the Mod Center; the code is on GitHub.

items.name: CaptureAge
items.what: Watch the recording with full vision of both sides, economy and army graphs. For understanding one specific loss.

items.name: AoE2 Insights
items.what: Profile, history and stats by civ and map. The minute-by-minute analysis is paid.

items.name: AoE2 Tech Tree
items.what: Tech tree of every civ, with cost and time of every unit and research.

items.name: AoE2 Companion
items.what: Mobile app with profile, live games and build orders.

qol.title: Quality-of-life mods
qol.intro: All in the game's Mod Center, free. They help you see better without changing the rules.

items.name: Improved Small Trees
items.what: Smaller trees: you can see villagers and enemies behind the forest.

items.name: Improved Tech Tree UI
items.what: Your civ's tech tree always at hand.

items.name: Grid mods
items.what: A grid on the ground to line up houses, walls and farms.

bo.intro: Pick the build you tried to follow. The site compares its milestones (buildings, researches, units and how many villagers you had at the time) with the recording. Which resource each villager went to is not stored in the recording.

focus.title: Training focus

goal.tcIdle: Keep the Town Center idle for less time
goal.firstMilitary: Get your first military unit out earlier

focus.why: {metric}: in {worse} of your last {total} games you were behind the median of {ref}, which is {target}. Your median in those games was {mine}.
focus.aboveNote: In your own division you are already at the median or better in everything. The target now is the division above.

tip.tcIdle: Press the Town Center hotkey and queue a villager every time you have 50 food, without waiting to bank more. Keeping two in the queue costs little and covers the moments you forget. Before aging up, make sure the Town Center will not sit empty.
tip.vils10: Villagers at 10:00 means a Town Center that never stops plus Loom at the right step of the build. Keep six to eight villagers on food (sheep, then boar and deer) before sending anyone to wood, and build the house before you hit the population cap.
tip.feudal: An early Feudal Age is a build order on autopilot: pick one, repeat it until it runs without thinking, and check every game with the build-order checker on the analysis page.
tip.vils15: Between Feudal and Castle the Town Center keeps producing. Queue a villager before researching the age and build the first farms while the research runs.
tip.castle: An early Castle Age depends on wood and gold in Feudal: four villagers on gold before the click and a Town Center that never stops. Compare your Feudal time: if it is already on target, the delay is in the stretch between the ages.
tip.vils20: After Castle Age, build the second and third Town Centers and keep all three queuing villagers. Place them next to wood and gold so nobody walks.
tip.firstMilitary: Build the barracks, archery range or stable right after clicking up to Feudal and queue the first unit as soon as the age arrives. One early unit holds the enemy scout and gives you information.
tip.imperial: An early Imperial Age needs a big economy: more villagers at 20:00, reseeded farms and steady gold. Train the villager count first and the age comes on its own.
tip.apm: Actions per minute go up with hotkeys: Town Center, villager, barracks and the idle-villager cycle on the keyboard, not the mouse. The hotkey trainers on the How to train page are for this.
